links.outcome: Algorithm AUC/sensitivity/specificity compared with clinician graders on same test set
links.effect: Algorithm matched or exceeded all independent clinician graders (AUC 0.92 vs optometrist labels, 0.93 vs expert panel labels); grader sensitivity 0.33-0.99, specificity 0.68-0.98.
links.quote: Algorithm performance matched or exceeded that of all independent clinician graders in detecting patient-level referable glaucoma based on LAC DHS optometrist (AUC = 0.92) or expert panel (AUC = 0.93) reference labels.

links.outcome: Variability of clinician grader accuracy and dependence on reference label source
links.effect: Clinician grader sensitivity (0.33-0.99) and specificity (0.68-0.98) ranged widely, unrelated to experience (p ≥ 0.49), showing inconsistent ground truth from single graders.
links.quote: Clinician grader sensitivity (range: 0.33-0.99) and specificity (range: 0.68-0.98) ranged widely and did not correlate with years of experience (p ≥ 0.49).

unlisted_practices: Training glaucoma detection algorithm on safety-net teleretinal screening data using patient-level labels from trained optometrist graders

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates a deep learning algorithm for detecting referable glaucoma from fundus photographs using a retrospective dataset from a safety net screening program, comparing it to clinician graders in a reader study setup.
